scenario: Finance processes 12,000 invoice pages a month. Dev proposes sending each page to a flagship model with vision and asking for the fields as JSON.
stem: What is the strongest argument for Document Intelligence's prebuilt invoice model instead?
options: Large models cannot read images
It is cheaper and predictable at volume, and it returns fixed fields with a confidence score and position for each, so thresholds and review screens are possible
It never makes mistakes
It needs no Azure subscription
explanation: Field-level confidence is what makes safe automation possible, and per-page pricing stays low at volume. The prebuilt model can still be wrong, which is why the threshold and review queue exist.

stem: How should confidence scores be used when automating extraction?
options: Ignore them; the service is accurate enough
Send everything below 1.0 to a person
Set a threshold per field: values above it flow through automatically and the rest go to a review screen, and adjust the threshold as results prove themselves
Average them across the document and reject low-scoring suppliers
explanation: Per-field thresholds let the confident majority flow through while a person checks the uncertain minority. A threshold of 1.0 sends everything to review, and ignoring scores lets mistakes post silently.

scenario: Delivery notes from the five largest suppliers each use their own fixed layout, and the prebuilt models miss key fields.
stem: What is the sensible next step?
options: Train a custom Document Intelligence model on labelled samples from each of those suppliers
Fine-tune a large language model on the delivery notes
Ask suppliers to switch to the prebuilt invoice format
Go back to manual typing
explanation: Custom extraction models learn a fixed layout from a handful of labelled examples and keep field-level confidence. Train on samples from every supplier you expect, not just one.

scenario: Service calls are transcribed so that complaint trends can be analysed. Callers often read out card numbers and addresses.
stem: What should happen before transcripts are stored?
options: Nothing, because the storage account is encrypted
Translate them, so the data is harder to read
Store only the audio
Run Language's PII detection to redact card numbers, addresses and names, then store the redacted text and summary
explanation: Encryption at rest does not stop people who can read the store from seeing card numbers. Redacting before storage keeps personal data out of every downstream copy, and storing only audio keeps the problem.

stem: Which task most needs a generative model rather than a task-specific service?
options: Reading totals from supplier invoices
Transcribing recorded calls
Summarising the themes across a week's reviews into a short note for the product team
Translating product pages into French
explanation: Finding and summarising themes needs judgement over varied text, which is what generative models are for. Reading fields, transcribing and translating are defined tasks with purpose-built, cheaper services.

scenario: The warehouse must keep reading delivery notes when its internet link drops for hours.
options: Run Document Intelligence in a container on the warehouse server; connected containers still report usage for billing
Cache the cloud service's responses in the browser
Switch to a flagship model, which works offline
There is no option; all Azure AI Services are cloud-only
explanation: Several AI services ship as containers for on-premises and edge use. Connected containers need only occasional connectivity to report usage, and fully disconnected containers exist for approved cases.

stem: Where does Content Understanding fit among the options?
options: It is the new name for Azure AI Speech
It uses generative models to extract fields you define from varied documents, images, audio and video, returning them to your schema with confidence scores
It trains a custom language model on your content
It filters harmful content from model outputs
explanation: It suits inputs too varied for one fixed layout. Unlike free-form prompting, it keeps a schema, confidence scores and where each value was found. Harmful-content filtering belongs to Content Safety.

scenario: A team plans to identify returning customers by face at store entrances, using a region chosen for its low price.
stem: What should you point out first?
options: Face identification is free
Nothing; any AI service is available in every region to every customer
Use Translator instead
Recognising individuals is available only to approved customers under Microsoft's responsible AI rules, raises serious privacy and legal questions, and features vary by region
explanation: Face identification is restricted for good reasons, and a use case like this needs legal and ethical review before any technical work starts. Regional availability varies for many AI features, so check it before choosing a region.
